significance: A Shiva temple about ten kilometres from Cooch Behar town whose linga stands in an underground sanctum beneath a squarish domed structure with a curved cornice. Its foundation is contested between several traditions, variously crediting Raja Jalpeswar, the Khen ruler Nilambar, and the Koch rulers Nara Narayan and Pran Narayan, and it draws large crowds at Maha Shivaratri.
story: Tradition tells that the demon king Banasura persuaded Shiva to come down to earth, and that when Banasura halted at Baneswar the god vanished, leaving a linga on the bank of the Bangti river.
